headline: Reich and states open talks on constitutional reform
summary: The first conference of Reich and state governments meets in Berlin to debate constitutional and administrative reform; it ends without agreement.

headline: Defense minister Geßler resigns over film scandal
summary: Otto Geßler steps down after it emerges that the navy secretly sank hidden funds into the failing Phoebus film company.

headline: Piscator stages Schwejk with Grosz's cartoon sets
summary: Erwin Piscator's Berlin production of The Good Soldier Schwejk uses George Grosz's projected drawings as scenery.

headline: Reichstag loosens tenants' protection against eviction
summary: A new tenant-protection law narrows safeguards against eviction, even as the housing shortage left by the war persists.

headline: German athletes return to the Olympics at St. Moritz
summary: The Winter Games in St. Moritz are the first Olympics with a German team since Germany was left out of the 1920 and 1924 Games.

headline: Berlin unveils a 100-million-mark farm aid plan
summary: The government answers rural distress with a large agriculture aid package, after protests in Schleswig-Holstein.

headline: Reichstag votes first funds for 'Armored Cruiser A'
summary: Over SPD and KPD opposition, the outgoing Reichstag approves a first installment for the navy's new armored ship, which becomes a fierce election issue.

headline: US law returns most German property seized in the war
summary: A new American act lets 80 percent of the German private assets seized in the war go back to their owners; the rest is held for US claims against Germany.

headline: Eisenstein's October opens in Moscow
summary: Sergei Eisenstein's film epic of the 1917 revolution premieres at the Bolshoi Theater; a shorter German version with a new score follows in Berlin in April.

headline: Reichstag dissolved early; election set for 20 May
summary: With the center-right coalition broken over a school bill, the Reichstag is dissolved ahead of schedule and new elections are set for 20 May; Marx's cabinet stays on meanwhile.

headline: Bremen crew makes first westbound Atlantic airplane flight
summary: Hermann Köhl, James Fitzmaurice and Baron von Hünefeld fly the Junkers Bremen from Ireland to Canada, against the prevailing winds.

headline: Schmeling wins the German heavyweight boxing title
summary: Max Schmeling's win makes him the country's top heavyweight, a first step toward a world title two years later.

headline: Nazis disrupt Stresemann's Munich election rally
summary: NSDAP supporters break up a campaign appearance by the foreign minister ahead of May's Reichstag vote.

headline: Social Democrats and Communists gain in Reichstag election
summary: The SPD wins 22 more seats and the KPD nine, while the nationalist DNVP and the moderate bourgeois parties lose ground.

headline: Italian airship Italia crashes returning from the Pole
summary: General Umberto Nobile's polar expedition ends in disaster when the airship goes down in the Arctic.

headline: Cologne opens Pressa, a world fair for the press
summary: The international exhibition showcases newspapers, printing and propaganda technique from across the world.

headline: Garbo's Anna Karenina opens to German audiences
summary: MGM's silent film Love, retitled for German cinemas, opens with Tolstoy's tragic ending rather than the happy one offered to some American theaters.

headline: Müller forms a Grand Coalition after Marx resigns
summary: SPD leader Hermann Müller becomes chancellor, heading a five-party cabinet from the Social Democrats to the BVP.

headline: Strauss opera Die ägyptische Helena opens in Dresden
summary: Richard Strauss's new opera, reworking the Helen of Troy myth, has its world premiere at the Semperoper.

headline: Chiang Kai-shek's forces take Peking
summary: The Nationalist army's capture of the old capital marks the nominal end of China's warlord era.

headline: Reichstag grants amnesty for political offenses
summary: Deputies vote to pardon a range of politically motivated crimes from the republic's turbulent early years.

headline: Germany back at the Summer Games, finishes second
summary: At the Amsterdam Games, Germany's first Summer Olympics since 1912, the German team wins ten gold medals and places second behind the United States.

headline: Comintern congress hardens Moscow's line on the SPD
summary: The Sixth World Congress in Moscow names social democrats the communists' chief enemy, a line that sets the KPD against the SPD.

headline: Kellogg-Briand Pact renounces war as policy
summary: Germany and fourteen other nations sign in Paris, renouncing war as a tool of national policy.

headline: SPD ministers back cruiser funds; party stays in coalition
summary: After the SPD ministers vote in cabinet to release armored-cruiser funds, the party's Reichstag group regrets the decision but rejects leaving the coalition.

headline: Brecht and Weill's Threepenny Opera opens in Berlin
summary: The Theater am Schiffbauerdamm premiere turns a beggars'-opera update into the decade's theatrical sensation.

headline: Liners Europa and Bremen are launched a day apart
summary: Launched in Hamburg and Bremen on 15 and 16 August, the two ocean liners are built to win back the transatlantic speed record for Germany.

headline: Fleming's mold finding points toward penicillin
summary: A London bacteriologist notices a mold killing bacteria in a lab dish, a discovery that will take years to reach patients.

headline: Hitler's Prussian speaking ban is lifted
summary: The Nazi leader regains the right to address public rallies in Germany's largest state.

headline: Communists cleared to petition against the cruiser
summary: The interior ministry allows a KPD-led signature drive against armored-cruiser funding to go forward.

headline: Nazi rally against the Dawes Plan turns violent
summary: An NSDAP mass meeting protesting war reparations ends in street fighting with communist counter-demonstrators.

headline: Hugenberg takes the DNVP hard right
summary: The press baron wins the nationalist party's chairmanship and pushes it toward flat opposition to the republic.

headline: Graf Zeppelin makes its first Atlantic crossing
summary: The new airship's first intercontinental trip, from Friedrichshafen to Lakehurst, New Jersey, draws wide attention on both sides of the Atlantic.

headline: Cruiser-referendum drive falls short of signatures
summary: A KPD-backed petition against armored-cruiser funding fails to gather enough support to force a vote.

headline: Ruhr employers lock out 200,000 ironworkers
summary: The region's iron and steel employers shut out their workforce in a wage dispute, the era's biggest lockout.

headline: Reichstag votes down SPD bid to halt the cruiser
summary: Deputies reject a Social Democratic motion to stop armored-cruiser construction, deepening coalition strain.

headline: Vossische Zeitung starts serializing Remarque's novel
summary: The Berlin daily begins running All Quiet on the Western Front in installments ahead of its book publication.

headline: Reichstag crushes a Nazi no-confidence bid on Stresemann
summary: The NSDAP's motion against the foreign minister fails by an overwhelming margin.

headline: Ruhr iron lockout ends as both sides accept arbitration
summary: The five-week lockout is lifted on 3 December after both sides agree to accept Interior Minister Severing's award, which follows on 21 December.

headline: Center Party turns right under new chairman Kaas
summary: Monsignor Ludwig Kaas wins the Center Party chair over two labor-wing rivals, and the Catholic party moves to the right.

headline: Powers agree on an expert panel to rework reparations
summary: Germany and six other powers agree to set up a committee of independent experts to draft a final reparations settlement.

headline: Unemployment passes two million in a hard winter
summary: Seasonal layoffs push the jobless count above two million by mid-January, a heavy load on the new unemployment insurance fund.

headline: Himmler named Reichsführer of the SS
summary: Heinrich Himmler takes command of the Nazi Party's small elite guard, then fewer than 300 men.

headline: Soviets expel Trotsky, deport him toward Turkey
summary: Stalin has his rival driven out of the USSR; Trotsky's exile carries him on to Constantinople.

headline: Remarque's war novel appears in bookshops
summary: All Quiet on the Western Front, already a newspaper sensation, is published as a book to enormous sales.

headline: Reichstag ratifies the pact renouncing war
summary: Deputies formally approve the Kellogg-Briand Pact that Germany signed the previous August.

headline: Vatican City is born under the Lateran Treaty
summary: Italy and the Holy See settle their long dispute over Rome, creating an independent Vatican state.

headline: Winter unemployment climbs past three million
summary: Joblessness tops three million in February, straining the insurance fund whose deficits will later help bring down the government.

headline: Germany's first sound feature film opens
summary: Walter Ruttmann's Melodie der Welt, a documentary set to music and sound effects, premieres in Berlin as Germany's first full-length sound film.

headline: General Motors buys control of Opel
summary: The American carmaker's purchase of Adam Opel AG ties a major German manufacturer to Detroit capital.

headline: Marshal Foch, Allied wartime commander, dies
summary: Ferdinand Foch, supreme Allied commander in 1918, who judged the Versailles treaty too lenient on Germany, dies in Paris.

headline: Prussia extends Berlin's rally ban to the whole state
summary: A ban on open-air political demonstrations, first imposed in Berlin in December 1928, goes statewide in March.

headline: Musil's play Die Schwärmer premieres in Berlin
summary: Robert Musil's 1921 drama finally reaches a Berlin stage, heavily cut and over the author's objections.

headline: Reichstag ratifies the ban on gas and germ warfare
summary: Germany formally joins the 1925 Geneva Protocol outlawing the use of poison gas and bacteriological weapons in war.

headline: Berlin police brace for banned May Day marches
summary: Officials warn of violence if communists defy the standing ban on open-air demonstrations for May Day.

headline: Bloody May: police and marchers clash across Berlin
summary: Communist-led May Day marches defy a standing ban; police gunfire over three days leaves dozens dead.

headline: Prussia bans the communist Red Front Fighters' League
summary: The paramilitary group is outlawed after Bloody May, with the ban extended nationwide within days.

headline: Berlin tentatively accepts a new reparations settlement
summary: German negotiators signal acceptance of the outline that will become the Young Plan, still weeks from signature.

headline: SPD congress in Magdeburg fights over the armored cruiser
summary: At the party congress, the left wing demands that SPD deputies, ministers and Chancellor Müller vote against the cruiser's second installment.

headline: Young Plan signed in Paris, reparations reset to 1988
summary: The new schedule replaces the Dawes Plan, spreading Germany's war reparations over fifty-eight years.

headline: Ramsay MacDonald becomes British prime minister
summary: Labour's return to power in London puts a more conciliatory figure at the head of German-British relations.

headline: Hindemith's opera Neues vom Tage opens in Berlin
summary: Paul Hindemith's comic opera, a satire of marriage, celebrity and the press, premieres at Berlin's Kroll Opera under Otto Klemperer.

headline: Reichstag passes the defense budget over SPD dissent
summary: Chancellor Müller and the SPD ministers back the military budget, cruiser funds included, against the votes of their own Reichstag group.

headline: Nationalists and Nazis unite against the Young Plan
summary: Hugenberg, Hitler and other right-wing leaders form a committee to force a referendum against the reparations plan.

headline: Farm leaders reject the Young Plan as unworkable
summary: The national farmers' committee says the plan's payments would exceed what the German economy can bear.

headline: Poincaré resigns; Briand returns as French premier
summary: The change in Paris puts Stresemann's reconciliation partner back at the head of the French government.

headline: Nazi party rally in Nuremberg ends in street fighting
summary: Columns of SA and SS men march at the NSDAP's four-day rally; clashes with communists and police leave dead and injured, and Jewish-owned shops are wrecked.

headline: The Hague conference opens on reparations and the Rhineland
summary: Allied and German delegations meet to finalize the Young Plan and set a timetable for leaving the Rhineland.

headline: Graf Zeppelin completes its round-the-world flight
summary: The airship's circumnavigation, starting and ending in New Jersey, is hailed as a triumph of German engineering.

headline: Soviet and Chinese forces clash on the Manchurian border
summary: The dispute over the Chinese Eastern Railway turns to fighting between Soviet troops and Zhang Xueliang's Manchurian army; a major Soviet offensive follows in the fall.

headline: Radical farmers bomb the Reichstag building
summary: A pre-dawn blast, tied to Schleswig-Holstein's Landvolk protest movement, shatters windows but hurts no one.

headline: Briand and Stresemann float a European federation
summary: The two foreign ministers raise the idea of closer European union at the League of Nations in Geneva.

headline: British troops begin an early exit from the Rhineland
summary: Under the deal struck at The Hague, the British garrison at Wiesbaden starts to leave; the last British troops go in mid-December.

headline: Landvolk bombing leader Claus Heim is captured
summary: Police arrest the farmers'-movement radical behind a string of bomb attacks on tax and district offices across the north.

headline: Foreign minister Stresemann dies suddenly at 51
summary: A massive stroke kills Gustav Stresemann, the architect of Germany's post-war reconciliation with the West.

headline: Wall Street's crash sends shockwaves through Germany
summary: The New York stock market collapse threatens the short-term American credit German banks and cities rely on.

headline: Curtius takes over as foreign minister
summary: Julius Curtius succeeds the late Stresemann, inheriting the unfinished Young Plan negotiations.

headline: Anti-Young-Plan petition narrowly forces a referendum
summary: The nationalist signature drive scrapes past the 10 percent threshold needed to put its Freedom Law to a public vote.

headline: Experts sign the statute for a new reparations bank
summary: Meeting at Baden-Baden, a committee of central bankers signs the draft statute of the Bank for International Settlements.

headline: Nazis win seats on Berlin's city council
summary: The NSDAP enters the capital's municipal assembly for the first time, with 13 of 225 seats.

headline: Reichstag overwhelmingly rejects the Freedom Law
summary: Deputies vote down the nationalist bill that would have repudiated the Young Plan and Versailles obligations.

headline: Occupation troops leave the Koblenz Rhineland zone
summary: The withdrawal, ahead of the original schedule, is a visible first fruit of the Young Plan settlement.

headline: Nationalist deputies quit the DNVP over Hugenberg's hard line
summary: About a dozen DNVP Reichstag members break away, protesting the chairman's alliance with the Nazis against the Young Plan.

headline: Nazis win six seats in Thuringia's state election
summary: The NSDAP takes 6 of the 53 seats, and the right-wing parties open coalition talks with it.

headline: Thomas Mann wins the Nobel Prize for Literature
summary: The award, cited for Buddenbrooks, is a rare moment of cultural pride amid the deepening economic gloom.

headline: Voters reject the nationalist referendum against Young Plan
summary: The Freedom Law plebiscite fails at the polls, but the campaign has boosted the once-marginal NSDAP.

headline: The Hague conference seals the Young Plan
summary: Powers at The Hague sign the Young Plan, with payments through 1988 totaling 112 billion marks, and the accord to leave the Rhineland.

headline: SA man Horst Wessel shot in his Berlin flat
summary: The Nazi storm-troop leader is wounded in a shooting tied to a dispute over his lodgings; he dies of it weeks later.

headline: Prussia bans open-air political rallies
summary: Interior Minister Albert Grzesinski bans outdoor assemblies to head off clashes between left- and right-wing groups.

headline: Frick becomes the first Nazi minister in a German state
summary: Wilhelm Frick takes charge of Thuringia's interior ministry, the NSDAP's first cabinet post anywhere.

headline: SA man Horst Wessel dies of his gunshot wounds
summary: Wessel dies on 23 February; Goebbels makes him a propaganda martyr, and a song Wessel wrote becomes the party's anthem.

headline: Farmers' cooperative body forms in Berlin
summary: Rival networks of rural cooperatives merge into one national Raiffeisen federation as farm prices keep sliding.

headline: Bauhaus design show travels to Essen
summary: An exhibition at the Folkwang Museum brings the school's modernist furniture and graphics to the Ruhr.

headline: Thuringia's Nazi minister bans Remarque's war novel
summary: Wilhelm Frick bars All Quiet on the Western Front from Thuringia's schools as unpatriotic.

headline: Reichsbank president Schacht quits over the Young Plan
summary: Hjalmar Schacht resigns rather than administer reparations terms he has come to oppose.

headline: Brecht and Weill's Mahagonny opens amid jeers in Leipzig
summary: The opera's premiere is disrupted by Nazi sympathizers hostile to its satire of capitalism.

headline: Reichstag passes the Young Plan into law
summary: A comfortable majority approves the reparations settlement, over nationalist and communist objections.

headline: Müller's coalition falls; Brüning named chancellor
summary: The Grand Coalition breaks apart over unemployment-insurance contributions; Hindenburg turns to Heinrich Brüning.

headline: The Blue Angel makes Marlene Dietrich a star
summary: Josef von Sternberg's film, Germany's prestige sound picture, premieres in Berlin with Dietrich as its cabaret singer.

headline: London naval treaty caps Britain, America and Japan
summary: The three sea powers agree new limits on warship tonnage, continuing the post-war arms-control effort.

headline: British authorities arrest Gandhi in India
summary: The independence leader is detained over his civil disobedience campaign, weeks after his Salt March to the sea.

headline: Briand proposes a European economic union
summary: The French foreign minister's plan for a federal Europe gets a cool, largely negative reception from Brüning's cabinet.

headline: Pabst's anti-war film Westfront 1918 opens in Berlin
summary: The unsparing trench-warfare drama adds to a wave of war films following Remarque's novel.

headline: Berlin bids to host the 1936 Olympic Games
summary: The capital puts itself forward at the International Olympic Committee's congress, a sign of the republic's confidence.

headline: Last French troops leave the Rhineland
summary: France withdraws its occupation garrison five years ahead of the Versailles schedule, cheered by crowds in the region.

headline: Nazis become Saxony's second-largest party
summary: The NSDAP wins 14 of 96 seats in the state election, trailing only the SPD and edging out the KPD.

headline: Schmeling wins the world heavyweight title on a foul
summary: Max Schmeling wins the vacant world heavyweight crown when Jack Sharkey is disqualified, the first German to hold it.

headline: Reichstag dissolved after budget decree is voted down
summary: Hindenburg dissolves the Reichstag after deputies vote to annul Brüning's Article 48 budget decree; elections are set for 14 September.

headline: Nationalists split as DNVP moderates quit Hugenberg
summary: A faction unhappy with Alfred Hugenberg's hard line breaks from the DNVP to form the Conservative People's Party.

headline: Uruguay beats Argentina to win the first World Cup
summary: Montevideo hosts the inaugural football World Cup; the host nation defeats Argentina 4-2 in the final.

headline: Bauhaus in Dessau dismisses director Hannes Meyer
summary: Dessau's mayor forces out Hannes Meyer over his left-wing politics; Ludwig Mies van der Rohe takes over the school.

headline: Freud's Goethe Prize draws attacks from the nationalist right
summary: Frankfurt awards Sigmund Freud its Goethe Prize; the Nazi press and völkisch critics attack the choice.

headline: Berlin SA men storm their own party's Gau office
summary: Walther Stennes's storm troopers, angry over pay and their say in the party, wreck Goebbels's Berlin headquarters and beat the SS guards.

headline: Nazi vote surges as Reichstag election reshapes politics
summary: The NSDAP jumps from 12 to 107 seats and the KPD gains too; the SPD stays the largest party but loses ground.

headline: Sound newsreels arrive in German cinemas
summary: Ufa's Tonwoche and the German edition of Fox Movietone launch newsreels with synchronized sound within days of each other.

headline: Berlin court jails Horst Wessel's killer and his accomplices
summary: Albrecht Höhler, the KPD member who shot Wessel, gets six years for manslaughter; several accomplices are also jailed.

headline: Pergamon Museum opens on Berlin's Museum Island
summary: Berlin's Pergamon Museum opens to the public, housing the reconstructed Pergamon Altar and Ishtar Gate.

headline: Brüning courts the Nazis as he looks for a majority
summary: Chancellor Brüning meets Hitler, Frick and Göring, testing whether the NSDAP could be drawn into cooperation.

headline: SPD votes save Brüning from no-confidence motions
summary: The new Reichstag rejects no-confidence motions from the KPD, NSDAP and DNVP; the SPD's votes keep Brüning in office.

headline: Berlin premiere for the operetta 'The White Horse Inn'
summary: Ralph Benatzky's operetta 'Im weißen Rössl' premieres at Berlin's Großes Schauspielhaus to popular acclaim.

headline: Austria's Social Democrats top the poll; Nazis win no seats
summary: The Social Democrats win the most seats, 72 of 165, but stay in opposition; the Nazis and Communists win none.

headline: India talks open in London without Gandhi at the table
summary: The Round Table Conference on India's future opens in London; Gandhi's Congress party stays away.

headline: Brüning bypasses parliament with a budget by decree
summary: Brüning issues a sweeping 'economic and financial security' emergency decree, setting 1931's budget without a Reichstag vote.

headline: Nazi disruption forces the war film off Berlin's screens
summary: Goebbels's followers riot at the Berlin premiere of 'All Quiet on the Western Front'; the film is banned days later.

headline: Ruhr mining wage talks collapse
summary: Talks on a new wage deal for Ruhr coal fail; the owners respond with notice to all 295,000 miners, effective 15 January.

headline: Communist-led strikes break out in the Ruhr coalfield
summary: The KPD calls strikes against the mass dismissals; an arbitration board then cuts miners' wages 6 percent and voids the notices.

headline: Röhm returns to head the storm troopers
summary: Hitler names Ernst Röhm, back from Bolivia, as the SA's chief of staff, tightening the paramilitary's discipline.

headline: Britain frees Gandhi to clear the way for talks
summary: British authorities release Mohandas Gandhi and other Congress leaders from prison, opening the way to talks with the viceroy.

headline: Prussia bans Goebbels's paper 'Der Angriff'
summary: Berlin police ban the Nazi paper 'Der Angriff', edited by Joseph Goebbels, for a stretch in early February.

headline: Right-wing deputies stage a walkout over Reichstag rules
summary: NSDAP and DNVP deputies leave the chamber in protest at new rules curbing debate, after failing to unseat Brüning.

headline: Pabst's 'Threepenny Opera' film opens in Berlin
summary: G. W. Pabst's screen version of Brecht and Weill's 'Die Dreigroschenoper' premieres in Berlin cinemas.

headline: Former Chancellor Hermann Müller dies in Berlin
summary: Hermann Müller, the SPD chancellor who led Germany's last majority cabinet, dies after surgery.

headline: Berlin and Vienna plan a customs union, alarming Paris
summary: Germany and Austria announce plans for a customs union; France sees a step toward forbidden political union.

headline: Hindenburg tightens the reins on assembly and the press
summary: A new emergency decree restricts public gatherings and gives authorities wider powers to muzzle newspapers.

headline: Unemployment nears five million as relief funds strain
summary: Joblessness approaches five million; only half the jobless draw insurance benefits, and the rest rely on crisis aid or local welfare.

headline: Spain's king goes into exile as a republic is declared
summary: After republicans sweep Spain's city elections, King Alfonso XIII leaves the country and a republic is proclaimed.

headline: Thuringia's Landtag removes its Nazi interior minister
summary: Wilhelm Frick, the NSDAP's first state minister, loses his Thuringian post after a no-confidence vote.

headline: Hitler dismisses his rebellious Berlin SA commander
summary: Hitler removes Walther Stennes as SA chief for eastern Germany; Stennes's men seize Goebbels's Berlin office, but the revolt soon collapses.

headline: New York opens the Empire State Building
summary: President Hoover dedicates the Empire State Building by remote switch; it stands as the world's tallest.

headline: France rejects the German-Austrian customs union plan
summary: The French Chamber rejects the plan, and at Britain's request the League Council refers it to the World Court.

headline: Fritz Lang's child-murderer film 'M' opens in Berlin
summary: Fritz Lang's 'M', starring Peter Lorre as a hunted killer, premieres to strong notices in Berlin.

headline: Berlin is chosen to host the 1936 Olympic Games
summary: The International Olympic Committee awards the 1936 Summer Games to Berlin over Barcelona.

headline: Hindenburg's decree cuts wages and benefits again
summary: A fresh emergency decree trims civil servants' pay, welfare payments, and unemployment benefits further.

headline: Hoover proposes a year's freeze on war debts
summary: US President Hoover calls for a one-year halt to reparations and war-debt payments; Brüning welcomes the relief.

headline: Fire destroys some 3,000 artworks in Munich's Glass Palace
summary: A blaze guts the Glass Palace exhibition hall; the losses include all 110 paintings in a show of German Romantics.

headline: Danatbank, one of Germany's biggest banks, collapses
summary: The Darmstädter und Nationalbank shuts its doors after a run set off by losses on loans to the failed textile firm Nordwolle, deepening the banking panic.

headline: Hindenburg shuts the banks by decree amid the panic
summary: A run on deposits forces a government-ordered bank holiday and currency controls across Germany.

headline: Powers meet in London to address Germany's finances
summary: A seven-power conference opens in London to discuss shoring up the German economy after the banking collapse.

headline: Bavaria bans political uniforms across the state
summary: A Munich police ban on political uniforms, issued at the start of the month, is widened to all of Bavaria on 10 July.

headline: Prussian referendum to dissolve its parliament fails
summary: A Nazi- and Communist-backed vote to dissolve the Prussian Landtag falls short of the turnout needed to pass.

headline: London conference sets the terms of the debt moratorium
summary: Delegates in London finalize how Hoover's one-year freeze on reparations and war debts will work in practice.

headline: Britain's crisis forces a National Government in London
summary: A run on the pound splits Britain's cabinet; a cross-party National Government forms to manage the crisis.

headline: Britain abandons the gold standard
summary: London takes the pound off gold, a shock that ripples through world currency and trade markets.

headline: SA men attack passers-by on Berlin's Kurfürstendamm
summary: SA squads roam the Ku'damm on the Jewish New Year, beating passers-by they take for Jews, smashing shop windows and storming a café.

headline: Hitler meets Ruhr industrialists seeking backers
summary: Hitler holds talks with steel and coal magnates including Fritz Thyssen, courting business money for the party.

headline: Ban lifted on the war film 'All Quiet on the Western Front'
summary: German censors lift the December 1930 ban on the anti-war film, allowing a cut version to be shown.

headline: Brüning reshuffles his cabinet at Hindenburg's demand
summary: Brüning resigns and is promptly reappointed with a more conservative cabinet, as Hindenburg pushes him rightward.

headline: Hindenburg receives Hitler for the first time
summary: President Hindenburg and Chancellor Brüning meet Hitler in Berlin, the Nazi leader's first audience with the president.

headline: Right-wing rivals unite at Bad Harzburg
summary: The NSDAP, DNVP, and Stahlhelm veterans rally together at Bad Harzburg, forming the 'Harzburg Front' opposition bloc.

headline: Foreign minister Curtius resigns over the customs union collapse
summary: Julius Curtius steps down as foreign minister after the failed bid for an Austro-German customs union.

headline: Editor Ossietzky jailed for exposing secret rearmament
summary: Carl von Ossietzky, editor of 'Die Weltbühne', is sentenced to eighteen months for revealing banned military aviation.

headline: NSDAP tops the poll in Hesse's state election
summary: The Nazis win a plurality in Hesse's Landtag election, extending their run of state-level gains.

headline: Prussia bans open-air political rallies
summary: Prussia's interior ministry outlaws outdoor demonstrations in a bid to curb the rising street violence.

headline: SPD and unions form the 'Iron Front' against the Nazis
summary: The Reichsbanner, trade unions, and the SPD found the Iron Front, answering the right's Harzburg Front with a republican bloc.

headline: Hugenberg's DNVP confirms its Harzburg pact with Hitler
summary: At a DNVP delegates' meeting, Hugenberg confirms the alliance with the Nazis that his party sealed at Bad Harzburg in October.

headline: New emergency decree orders cuts in wages, prices, and rents
summary: Brüning's fourth emergency decree rolls wages, prices, and rents back to 1927 levels and cuts interest rates, deepening the deflation.

headline: Unemployment closes 1931 at 5.6 million
summary: Year-end figures put registered joblessness at 5.6 million, with many more uncounted.

headline: Brüning says Germany cannot resume paying reparations
summary: With the Hoover moratorium running out, Brüning tells the British and French ambassadors that Germany cannot restart reparations.

headline: Wels wary of extending Hindenburg's term without an election
summary: SPD chairman Otto Wels tells Brüning he doubts the chancellor's plan to have the Reichstag prolong Hindenburg's term and spare him a popular vote.

headline: Nazi students bar Jewish classmates from Berlin lecture halls
summary: Nazi students physically block Jewish classmates from Berlin university halls; four Jewish students are injured.

headline: World disarmament conference opens in Geneva
summary: Delegates from dozens of nations open the League of Nations' World Disarmament Conference at Geneva.

headline: Unemployment tops six million, a third of the workforce
summary: Official figures show more than six million Germans out of work, the depression's worst point yet.

headline: Hitler announces he will run against Hindenburg for president
summary: Goebbels reveals Hitler's candidacy for the presidency, setting up a direct contest with Hindenburg.

headline: Winter Olympics open at Lake Placid
summary: The third Winter Olympic Games open in Lake Placid, New York, with only 17 nations taking part, down from 25 in 1928.

headline: Hindenburg falls just short of a majority against Hitler
summary: In the presidential vote's first round, Hindenburg takes 49.6 percent to Hitler's 30.1 and Thälmann's 13.2, forcing a runoff.

headline: The Lindbergh baby is kidnapped in New Jersey
summary: The infant son of aviator Charles Lindbergh is abducted from the family's home, gripping world headlines.

headline: Riefenstahl's 'The Blue Light' opens in Berlin
summary: Leni Riefenstahl's mountain film 'Das blaue Licht', which she directed and starred in, premieres in Berlin.

headline: Germany marks the centenary of Goethe's death
summary: Commemorations across the country mark 100 years since Johann Wolfgang von Goethe died in Weimar on 22 March 1832.

headline: Hindenburg wins re-election, holding off Hitler
summary: In the presidential runoff Hindenburg takes 53 percent to Hitler's 36.8, with Thälmann far behind.

headline: Reichsbank president Luther grazed by a gunman's bullet
summary: Hans Luther is lightly wounded when a lawyer and an accomplice fire on him at Berlin's Potsdam station, apparently over the bank's monetary policy.

headline: Brüning's government bans the SA and SS nationwide
summary: After police find coup plans, and under pressure from Prussia and other states, an emergency decree dissolves Hitler's SA and SS.

headline: Nazi gains cost Braun's coalition its Prussian majority
summary: Sweeping NSDAP gains in Prussia, Bavaria, and other states leave Otto Braun's government without a majority.

headline: May Day marches turn violent between Nazis and Communists
summary: Clashes break out around May Day rallies as Nazi and Communist paramilitaries fight in several cities.

headline: Defense minister Groener resigns under army pressure
summary: Wilhelm Groener quits as defense minister after backing the SA ban costs him the Reichswehr's confidence.

headline: NSDAP wins an outright majority in tiny Oldenburg
summary: The Nazis take an absolute majority in the small state of Oldenburg's Landtag election.

headline: Brüning falls; Hindenburg asks Papen to form a cabinet
summary: Hindenburg withdraws his confidence and Brüning resigns. On 31 May Franz von Papen is asked to form a cabinet, with Schleicher to take defense.

headline: Reichstag dissolved at Papen's request; election set for July
summary: Hindenburg dissolves parliament at new chancellor Franz von Papen's request and calls fresh Reichstag elections for 31 July.

headline: Powers meet at Lausanne to settle reparations for good
summary: Germany and its creditors open talks at Lausanne aiming to end reparations payments for good.

headline: Strasser gives the first Nazi speech on German radio
summary: Gregor Strasser says the NSDAP wants no persecution of Jews but a German leadership free of 'Jewish spirit', and would not shy from war as a last resort.

headline: Eighteen die in Altona as an SA march sparks street fighting
summary: An SA march through Communist Altona ends in gunfire; eighteen people are killed, most shot by police.

headline: Papen ousts Prussia's government by decree
summary: Hindenburg makes Papen Reich commissioner for Prussia by decree; Otto Braun's government is removed under martial law in Berlin.

headline: Lausanne talks end reparations in all but name
summary: The Lausanne conference closes with reparations cut by some 90 percent to one final payment, which Germany never makes.

headline: NSDAP becomes the largest party in the Reichstag
summary: The Nazis win 37.3 percent in the July election, far ahead of the SPD, but short of a majority.

headline: Hitler turns down the vice-chancellorship, wants full power
summary: Papen offers Hitler the vice-chancellorship; Hitler refuses, demanding the chancellorship itself.

headline: SA men sentenced to death for the Potempa killing
summary: Five storm troopers are condemned to death for beating a Communist worker to death in Upper Silesia; Hitler backs them publicly.

headline: Dessau's council votes to shut the Bauhaus school
summary: A Nazi-backed council majority in Dessau votes to close the Bauhaus, effective that October.

headline: New special courts make political killing a capital crime
summary: A decree creates fast-track courts and toughens penalties for politically motivated violence and murder.

headline: New Reichstag votes down Papen before he can dissolve it
summary: Deputies pass a no-confidence motion against Papen 512 to 42; he dissolves the chamber anyway, forcing a new vote.

headline: Papen's wage-cutting economic program becomes law by decree
summary: An emergency decree enacts Papen's plan to cut wages and taxes in a bid to spur hiring.

headline: Stahlhelm rally draws some 150,000 to Berlin
summary: The Stahlhelm veterans' league holds its front soldiers' day at Berlin's Tempelhof field, drawing veterans, soldiers, and right-wing supporters.

headline: Top court splits the difference on Papen's Prussian coup
summary: The Staatsgerichtshof rules the takeover partly lawful but Braun's removal unjustified; his ministers keep their standing while Papen's men run Prussia.

headline: NSDAP youth rally draws over 100,000 to Potsdam
summary: The Hitler Youth and NSDAP hold a mass rally in Potsdam, one of the movement's largest shows of strength yet.

headline: Austria bans both Nazi and Social Democrat street parades
summary: Chancellor Dollfuss's government bans political marches in Austria, curbing Nazi and Social Democrat shows of force alike.

headline: Communists and Nazis both back a Berlin transit strike
summary: A wildcat strike against wage cuts hits Berlin's transport network, with Communist and Nazi unions unusually aligned.

headline: NSDAP loses ground but stays the largest Reichstag party
summary: A second 1932 election cuts the Nazi vote share from 37 to 33 percent, though they remain far ahead of the SPD.

headline: Papen resigns, unable to find a Reichstag majority
summary: Franz von Papen steps down as chancellor after talks show no majority will tolerate him; Schleicher has pressed him to go.

headline: Roosevelt elected US president on a recovery platform
summary: Franklin D. Roosevelt defeats Hoover in a landslide, promising relief from the depression.

headline: Schleicher becomes chancellor, plans to split the Nazis
summary: Hindenburg names General Kurt von Schleicher chancellor; he hopes to peel off the NSDAP's left wing.

headline: Strasser quits his party posts after clashing with Hitler
summary: Gregor Strasser resigns his NSDAP offices after Hitler rejects his idea of entering a Schleicher cabinet.

headline: Five powers recognize Germany's right to equal armaments
summary: A Geneva declaration grants Germany 'equality of rights' in principle at the disarmament conference.

headline: Schleicher rolls back Papen's wage cuts to court unions
summary: The new government cancels Papen's wage reductions, hoping to win trade-union and SPD tolerance.

headline: NSDAP rebounds sharply in tiny Lippe's state election
summary: The Nazis take 39.5 percent in Lippe, a small state vote they use to claim their decline has reversed.

headline: Papen brokers backroom talks between Hitler and Hindenburg's circle
summary: Papen meets Hitler secretly, working with Hindenburg's son and state secretary to arrange a Hitler chancellorship.

headline: Schleicher resigns after Hindenburg denies him emergency powers
summary: Chancellor Schleicher quits after 57 days when Hindenburg refuses to let him rule by decree and dissolve the Reichstag.

headline: Hindenburg names Hitler chancellor
summary: Hindenburg appoints Hitler chancellor of a coalition cabinet; SA, SS and Stahlhelm parade by torchlight through Berlin.

headline: Hitler has Hindenburg dissolve the Reichstag
summary: Days after taking office, Hitler secures a Reichstag dissolution from Hindenburg, with elections set for March.

headline: Nazi pressure pushes Kollwitz and Mann from the Academy
summary: Käthe Kollwitz and Heinrich Mann resign from the Prussian Academy of Arts under Nazi pressure over a leftist appeal.

headline: Fire guts the Reichstag; a Dutch council communist is blamed
summary: A fire destroys the Reichstag's plenary hall; police arrest Marinus van der Lubbe at the scene.

headline: Emergency decree suspends civil liberties after the fire
summary: Hindenburg signs a decree suspending freedom of the press and assembly and protection from arbitrary arrest, used at once against the left.

headline: NSDAP wins 43.9 percent, short of a majority on its own
summary: In the last multi-party election, the Nazis win 43.9 percent; with DNVP allies they scrape a bare majority.

headline: Hindenburg presides over the ceremonial 'Day of Potsdam'
summary: A staged ceremony at Potsdam's garrison church links Hitler's new government to Prussian tradition, with Hindenburg presiding.

headline: First concentration camps open at Dachau and elsewhere
summary: Bavarian police open a camp at Dachau for political prisoners; similar camps appear in other states.

headline: Reichstag passes the Enabling Act, sidelining itself
summary: With KPD deputies arrested or in hiding and SA men lining the hall, deputies pass the Enabling Act 444-94; only the SPD votes no.
